taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: stems erect or decumbent at base, usually simple, 1 dm to 6 dm high.

traits.life_span.note: A perennial, as the photos' clumps and Abrams's account of its creeping, mat-forming typical form (1951 p. 628) show.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: leafy stems, the leaves along them.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Opposite, as in the family (Abrams 1951) and the photos: the species account does not say.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: leaves often 3 cm to 5 cm long; the typical form's smaller.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Blades 1 cm to 2.5 cm broad, about two to three times as long as broad, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 224577623, 191755313, 67283787, 294209716, 316745803, 4953611, 103964311, 119034365): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: narrowed to a short or elongated petiole, the upper leaves nearly sessile; set from 0 for those.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: leaves ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: entire or irregularly and remotely toothed.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: spikes terminal, their bracts orbicular or broadly ovate, green or often tinged with purple.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: spikes 2 cm to 5 cm long.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: 20 to 50 flowers, buds and calyces in the dense spike, a few rings open at a time, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 224577623, 191755313, 67283787, 294209716, 316745803, 4953611, 103964311, 119034365): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: corolla about twice as long as the calyx: a two-lipped tube.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: corolla 10 mm to 20 mm long; the typical form's 3 mm to 10 mm.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 628, Prunella vulgaris subsp. lanceolata: corolla violet or rarely white; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.fruit_type.note: Four nutlets, as in the family (Abrams 1951): the species account does not describe its fruit.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: flowering May to September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: green to purplish square stems; lance-shaped green leaves in pairs; a dense, squarish spike of violet two-lipped flowers among purple-tinged bracts.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for self-heal from Abrams's description and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). Its inflorescence is drawn as one cluster at each stem's tip, sized by the traits, so the stem ends where the cluster begins. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.26 m tall at 3 years in the open, within the flora's range. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
